_comment: sim/output-swing as a `klt sim` request: ONE-POINT NATIVE-CAPABILITY PROTOTYPE (issue #100, startable subset). Not an envelope for T1 item 5.
Point: mos_tt (+ cornerCAP.lib cap_typ) / 27 C / VDD 1.20 V, Vcm = VDD/2 = 0.60 V. The 45-point grid is deliberately NOT declared here (deferred work, sim/output-swing/README.md).
Circuit: tb_swing.body.spice, the same test circuit as ../testbench/tb_swing.spice.tmpl (one .include of design/netlist/opamp_core.spice).
vcm sweeps WITH vdd by index (klt supply_v semantics), so Vcm = VDD/2 at every corner, as in the harness.
Ratified row (spec/target-spec.md section 2, [DR-2]): headroom >= 251 mV from VDD, >= 141 mV from VSS, tracking span >= 0.571 V, -6 dB incremental-gain criterion, CL = 2 pF, unloaded.
The three ratified numbers are three independent `expr` measurements carrying the LITERAL bounds as `limits`: headroom_hi_v, headroom_lo_v, swing_span_v.

Estimator = the harness's sampled definition (run_swing_sweep.sh): segment gain g[i] = dVout/dVid between adjacent samples; peak = first max; the tracking region is the contiguous run of segments around the peak with g >= 0.5*peak; the bounds are the extreme Vout over the region's endpoint samples (segments lo..hi -> samples lo..hi+1).

In ngspice vector algebra, inside klt's own expr path: G = (v(out)[1,5000]-v(out)[0,4999])/(v(id)[1,5000]-v(id)[0,4999]) (5000 segments of the 5001-sample sweep); pk_idx = first index of vecmax(G); lo_idx = 1 + last index < pk_idx with G < 0.5*gpk (0 if none); hi_idx = (first index > pk_idx with G < 0.5*gpk) - 1 (4999 if none). Comparisons are written `lt`/`gt` because `<`/`>` are I/O redirection in ngspice's command line. Scalars (not vectors) are the only thing klt can print, so each stage is reduced to a scalar and referenced by name by the next expr.

lo_idx >= 1 and hi_idx <= 4998 reproduce the harness's 'linear region touches the window edge' rejection (len(g)-1 = 4999) as graded limits; gpk_vv >= 10 V/V is its 'plausible peak gain' rule; mono_min_dv_v >= -1e-9 V is its monotonic-curve rule. These are integrity checks, not ratified rows.

KNOWN DIFFERENCE FROM THE HARNESS: the harness centres the +-25 mV fine window on the interpolated Vout = Vcm crossing found by a coarse pass. A klt request cannot centre a sweep on a measured value (analysis.args are literal), so this request sweeps a FIXED window Vid = -10 mV .. +40 mV at 10 uV (5001 samples). The harness record's crossings span 11.4-21.9 mV over the whole grid, so a fixed window centred at 15 mV keeps every crossing >= 18 mV inside both edges; the coarse pass (clip levels, crossing) is not part of any ratified row and is not reproduced.
Solver tolerance: ngspice default, no .options reltol/abstol/vntol (DR-0005). ngspice_init raises printed digits only.
backend: local -- a single operating point. The shared dispatch host does not run grids; the 45-point work is deferred and must use the batch backend.
